_comment: THE table of expected versions, for all seven repositories. One table, here.
There is no pnpm catalog across the seven repositories — that is the limit of the
multi-repository layout, and it is accepted. The substitute is this table plus the
`arthome-check-versions` gate, NOT a hope. Seven autonomous package.json files would
be seven parallel literal tables under a common name: fault E2, applied to versions.
A — exact pin; a major bump is handled as a contract change. What belongs here is
what SEVERAL repositories must see the same way AT RUNTIME. Membership test:
if two repositories hold two different versions at the same time, does
something break in a way that is hard to diagnose? zod: yes. react: no (one
B — exact pin, bumped in the order of section 7.3.
C — range, bumped as they come. The lockfile is the record.
Verified on 2026-09-21 against registry.npmjs.org. THIS TABLE GOES STALE:
section 7.5 gives the commands that rebuild it.
⚠ A version bump pins a version that is ALREADY MATURE, never the day's — see
section 7.6. Pinning the day's latest guarantees minimumReleaseAge refuses it,
which is exactly what happened at the first install of this repository.

node.why: Intersection of the four floors. Angular 22 is the most demanding (^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26); RN 0.87 asks for ^22.13 || ^24.3 || >=26; ESLint 10 for ^20.19 || ^22.13 || >=24; @nestjs/cli for >=20.11. Node 24 'Krypton' is LTS; 26 is not yet.

pnpm.why: packageManager makes Corepack install the right version. minimumReleaseAge has defaulted to 1440 since pnpm 11.

A._why: Shared at runtime by several repositories. A major bump is a contract change.

zod.why: Runtime dependency shared by seven services and five applications. A peerDependency of @arthome/contracts, exactly pinned. Two zod copies in one process means two schema registries and unintelligible validation errors. Settled by the project lead.

typescript.why: One version per repository, and the same across all seven. Angular's hard ceiling (@angular/compiler-cli peer >=6.0 <6.1), joined by nest build (aborts on TS 7) and by typescript-eslint (peer >=4.8.4 <6.1.0). Nothing pushes upward: react-native has no typescript peer and @types/react accepts TS 5.1+.

B._why: Tooling that decides whether the build passes. Exact pin, bumped in the order of section 7.3.

eslint.why: A forced, dated divergence: @react-native/eslint-config@0.87.1 has peer `eslint ^8.0.0 || ^9.0.0` — not 10. Exit condition: a release of that preset accepting ESLint 10. eslintrc no longer exists in 10; the config is looked up from the linted file's directory upward.

@eslint/js.why: Must track eslint's major, which is why it is a peerDependency of @arthome/tooling and not a dependency.

prettier.why: Prettier 4 is in alpha (4.0.0-alpha.13). We stay on 3.x.

eslint-config-prettier.why: Dedicated flat entry point since 10.1.1: import `eslint-config-prettier/flat`, and put it LAST. Handles @stylistic rules since 10.0.0.

typescript-eslint.why: Peer typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0: this is the fleet's real ceiling. The TS 7 support request (issue #12518) was closed 'not planned' for lack of a TypeScript 7 API; it is expected in 7.1.

vitest.why: Angular 22 pins vitest ^4.0.8. This is why @arthome/tooling/vitest exports a bare object and imports nothing from vitest.

turbo.why: Task cache only. The five applications have none: a single-application repository has no task graph to cache. No Nx, in any of the seven.

forbidden._why: Installing any of these cancels a decision. The gate says so before review does.
forbidden.eslint-plugin-prettier: Forbidden: running Prettier as an ESLint rule is the very setup that CREATES the conflicts we are avoiding (section 3.3).
forbidden.prettier-plugin-organize-imports: Forbidden: would make Prettier sort imports, competing with import-x/order.
forbidden.@stylistic/eslint-plugin: Forbidden: gives formatting back to ESLint, which is what eslint-config-prettier exists to switch off.
forbidden.eslint-plugin-react-compiler: Do not install: last published 2025-08-15, never left RC. Its rules live in eslint-plugin-react-hooks.
forbidden.@biomejs/biome: Ruled out (D-013): it is the framework plugins — Angular template lint, React hooks and compiler rules, eslint-config-next — that catch the real faults, and Biome has no such ecosystem.
forbidden.nx: No Nx (README section 3): its generators, executors and migrations become a project inside the project.
forbidden.husky: No: core.hooksPath plus two ten-line hooks do the same work without three packages to maintain in seven copies (section 8.4).
forbidden.@commitlint/cli: Same reason: the commit-msg hook fits in ten lines.
